entry.v: core library version that produced the entry

coreToPage.description: A core instance announces itself on window.__COMVI__ at construction time when the devtools capability is present in its module graph and exposeGlobal is on (default true in browsers). In 0.4 the root entry always carried that capability. From 0.5 the single entry is the base host, so the capability arrives through the devtools() installer, attachDevtools, or a plugin installer that ensures devtools (in-context-editor); an app that composes none of them is invisible to the extension by construction, not by failure.
probeOrder: Array.isArray(g) -> g.push({v, i}) — raw v2 queue array, or a consumer's array-masquerading hook whose OWN push/remove shadow Array.prototype

typeof g.push === 'function' && typeof g.remove === 'function' -> g.push({v, i}) — v2 hook object, including dual-protocol hooks that also expose register; probed BEFORE legacy so new/new never downgrades to v1
typeof g.register === 'function' -> g.register(instanceId, instance) — register WITHOUT remove means a genuine v1 legacy registry; two-arg call so its get(id) resolves
!g -> window.__COMVI__ = [{v, i}] — install a fresh queue array
truthy non-conforming global -> left untouched, exposure skipped (never clobber)
coreToPage.removal: destroy() removes identity-based and probes in the SAME order as exposure: Array.isArray(g) -> a masquerading hook's OWN remove (own property, callable) gets g.remove(entry), otherwise indexOf/splice of the SAME entry object; then a non-array hook -> g.remove(entry); then legacy registry -> g.unregister(instanceId). Array.isArray FIRST is load-bearing: a page that extends Array.prototype with a remove(index) polyfill would otherwise be handed the entry OBJECT, which coerces to index 0 and splices someone else's live entry with nothing thrown. All discovery and removal is wrapped in try/catch — it must never break construction or destroy.
coreToPage.instanceIds: The default id is `comvi-<n>`, counted once per PAGE: the sequence lives in a `Symbol.for("comvi.core.instanceCounter")` slot on globalThis, so two copies of core on one page (CDN global plus bundled npm copy, or a binding pinned to another patch) continue one sequence instead of both minting `comvi-1`. Minting never reads `window.__COMVI__`: an id is chosen before the protocol is probed, so a hostile hook can neither throw out of construction nor make minting spin. An explicitly passed instanceId is used as given and may still collide, which the consumer dedupes on drain (see pageToExtension.idCollisions). `instanceId` is public: it appears on the instance and in the extension's ActivateResult.

pageToExtension.description: The consumer (in-context editor / Chrome extension) MUST drain-and-swap on boot: if window.__COMVI__ is an array, SWAP the global to its hook object FIRST, then drain the snapshot ({v, i} envelopes AND bare legacy instances). The swapped-in hook implements BOTH protocols: v2 (push/remove) and v1 legacy (register/unregister/get/instances view), so an old core landing later still attaches via register.
pageToExtension.hookShape: Object.assign([], { __comviEditorHook: true, push, remove, register, unregister, get, instances, version }) — array-masquerading so new core's Array.isArray-first probe routes through the hook's OWN push. Do not drop the array masquerade or reorder core's probe independently: they are a matched pair.
pageToExtension.markerRule: The hook carries `__comviEditorHook === true` so that whichever consumer installs first (in-context editor or extension detector) is REUSED by the other instead of swapping again. It is not proof of a hook: it is page-writable, and a page that pollutes Object.prototype.__comviEditorHook marks every object. A consumer MUST therefore validate requiredMembers before adopting a marked global, MUST probe Array.isArray BEFORE the marker (so a polluted prototype cannot make a raw queue array look like an installed hook), and MUST read the marker and the entry's `i` as OWN properties rather than with `in`. A marked global that fails requiredMembers is treated as whatever it otherwise looks like — a v1 legacy registry if it duck-types as one, else a truthy non-conforming global: left untouched, never adopted, never read, and never a thrown error.
pageToExtension.idCollisions: Consumer hooks key instances on `instance.instanceId`, so two cores that announced the same id must not overwrite one another. track() DEDUPES a colliding id, tracking the later instance under `<id>#<n>` (suffix appended to the ORIGINAL id, never to an already-suffixed one) and warning on the console, so both instances stay discoverable and countable. The deduped instance is addressable by the id it announced only while that is unambiguous: get(id) falls back to the single `<id>#<n>` entry when nothing holds the exact key, and returns undefined when two or more do, in which case the caller must name the deduped key. remove()/untrack() delete the map slot ONLY while it still holds THAT instance, and unregister(id) resolves the instance that CLAIMED the id through register(id, instance) before falling back to whoever holds the key, so neither can evict a different live instance.
pageToExtension.legacyRegistryBoot: If the pre-existing global is the v1 registry object (register fn / instances Map), read its instances map into the hook, then swap; keep a COMVI_READY listener on the drained legacy object as the v1 shim.

versionPairing.old-core+new-extension: supported — the extension's legacy shim reads .instances and COMVI_READY, and its dual-protocol hook accepts register()
versionPairing.new-core+old-extension: UNSUPPORTED — the one broken pairing; the old extension never drains the queue array. Release notes pin the minimum extension version.
versionPairing.old-core+new-core-same-page: supported — new core detects the legacy object (register without remove) and calls register(id, instance); the new extension's hook speaks both protocols. Ids may collide (old core also minted `comvi-<n>`); the hook's dedupe and identity-safe removal keep both instances discoverable (see pageToExtension.idCollisions).
versionPairing.new-core+new-core-same-page: supported — two copies of new core (CDN global plus bundled npm copy, or a binding on another patch) both push onto one queue/hook. The second copy skips an id a consumer hook already tracks, and a consumer draining a raw queue dedupes colliding ids, so both instances stay discoverable and destroying one leaves the other tracked.
